---
title: "Scope & Eligibility"
---

## Purpose

The Pharmacometrics Benchmarks repository is being developed as a curated, public collection of pharmacometric benchmark datasets to facilitate reproducible comparisons across modeling methodologies. The Benchmarking Datasets Working Group of the AI/ML SIG is developing it, with hosting under ISoP planned.

Content is openly accessible to both ISoP members and the broader scientific community.

---

## Two Goals

All submissions fall under one of the two goals. The goal determines the review track, effort bar, and publication pathway.

### Goal 1 — "Generic" Benchmarks

> *Maintain a curated, public repository of generic benchmark datasets to facilitate performance comparisons across novel pharmacometric methodologies.*

**Intended for:**

- Teaching cases and educational datasets
- Datasets intended for use in agentic or automated workflow evaluations ("agentic datasets")
- Unit-test style submissions isolating a single modeling phenomenon, such as sparse sampling, mixed dosing, or high covariate missingness
- Datasets with moderate complexity and limited novelty requirements

Note that this repository provides datasets only. Designing an agentic evaluation framework is out of scope here and is better suited to the Agentic WG, which may nonetheless make heavy use of these datasets in its evaluations.

**Review:** Minimal structural review. Novelty bar is not high, but must be justified (see [Novel and Motivated](#novelty-and-motivation)).

**Planned outcome:** Accepted submissions will be listed on the website and assigned a DOI once the archival process is in place.


---

### Goal 2 — Grand Challenges

> *Curate highly realistic datasets for specific pharmacometric problems ("grand challenges") that embody challenges encountered in real-world drug development, to raise awareness and promote novel methodologies to solve the field's big problems.*

**Intended for:**

- Datasets targeting complex, realistic drug-development scenarios — by submitters who have encountered a real-world problem that current methods cannot address effectively
- Multi-task benchmarks with clinical relevance
- Submissions designed for community competitions and rankings
- Datasets where the problem itself is the contribution (comparable to CASP / protein folding challenges in biology)

**Proposed review:** Editorial triage, then full scientific peer review in addition to structural review. A possible publication pathway with *Quantitative Medicine* is being explored; it is not yet established.

**Planned outcome:** Accepted submissions will be listed on the website and assigned a DOI once the archival process is in place. Featured status and inclusion in future benchmark suites may be offered.

---

## Eligibility Criteria

A submission is in scope if it meets all of the following, regardless of goal:

### 1. Pharmacometric in nature

The dataset must be appropriate for pharmacometric modeling — pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, exposure-response, or closely related quantitative clinical pharmacology tasks. Coverage across PK, PD, QSP, and novel data types (imaging, text, omics, all therapeutic modalities) is explicitly welcomed.

### 2. Well-documented

The submission must include:

- A generative process description for synthetic data, or a scenario and provenance description for other data
- A [yspec-style YAML data dictionary](https://github.com/metrumresearchgroup/yspec) for all variables
- A train/test split with documented rationale

### 3. Associated tasks

Each dataset should come with pre-defined tasks by the submitter. Ideally, these tasks will reflect real drug-development decisions (model selection, dose optimization, exposure-response characterization, etc.). Similar to the overall requirements on dataset novelty, this can be simpler for generic submissions (e.g. RMSE) and should be strongly motivated by real situations for the "grand challenge" datasets. Each task must have a defined metric and output format. See the [Submission Guide](submission-guide.qmd) for the task schema.

### 4. Novel and motivated {#novelty-and-motivation}

Submissions must include a **"letter to the editor" style motivation** — a dedicated section in the submission that:

- States why this dataset should be added to the repository
- Lists the most similar existing datasets (in this repository or elsewhere)
- Explains concretely how this submission is different enough to warrant inclusion

For Goal 1 submissions, one paragraph is sufficient. For Goal 2 submissions, a fuller justification is expected.

Reviewers will use this section to assess novelty. Novelty is inherently subjective; the letter-style format makes the reasoning transparent and auditable.

### 5. Shareable under the repository license

Submitters must have permission to share the data under the MIT license used by this repository. Retain the copyright and license notice when redistributing content. We also ask users to cite the datasets they use.

---

## Additional expectations for grand challenges

Grand challenges should reflect realistic clinical or drug-development conditions, including sampling, relationships among variables, and potential dropout or missingness where relevant. They should generally include repeated measurements over time. A non-longitudinal modality such as imaging can be considered case by case if the submission explains its pharmacometric relevance and why the benchmark belongs in this collection.

These expectations do not exclude focused, simpler Goal 1 benchmarks that isolate a single phenomenon.

## Recognition for Contributors

We want contributing a benchmark to be rewarding in proportion to the effort put in.

**The intended process for accepted submissions includes:**

- A DOI to make the dataset citable, once an archival process is in place
- A stable page in the collection

**Goal 2 submissions may additionally receive:**

- **A possible publication pathway** with *Quantitative Medicine*, subject to agreement with the journal
- **Possible ACoP spotlight** — a presentation opportunity through the AI/ML SIG, subject to its steering committee's discretion and event plans.
